events.body:
C1: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 873 m at 22:36:00 and he never came within 200 m of it at any time, so the arrival condition for a no-show charge is not met. [F1] [NS-1 NS-2]
C2: The platform itself never recorded the driver at the pickup point — driver_arrived_at is null — so there is no arrival confirmation on the record, whether by driver tap or platform auto-detect. [F4] [NS-1]
C3: The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 22:37:20 while 1000 m from the pickup point, and stayed within 200 m of it for 0 seconds after the tap, so NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both fail. [F5] [NS-1 NS-2]
C4: From 22:37:00 to 22:42:00 the driver was stationary 1000 m from the pickup point, so the waiting that preceded his 22:42:00 cancellation was not waiting at the pickup point; his written claim that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the GPS record and by the system timeline. [F2 F3 F12] [NS-1 NS-2]
C5: At 22:38:00 the rider messaged that she was at the pickup point and saw no car, which matches the GPS record that no car was ever within 200 m, while the driver's message at 22:37:00 asserted a pick-up that the record shows never happened. [F1 F8 F9] [NS-2]

[F5 F17] [NS-2 RD-6]
C8: No traffic incident or congestion record exists on the route during the trip window, so nothing external explains the driver's failure to reach the pickup point; light rain of 1.8 mm does not place the driver 873 m away. [F13 F14 F15] [RD-4]

events.title: Driver Advocate brief: 7 claims (1 void)
events.body:
D1: The rider was never charged a no-show fee in error on any basis the driver can be blamed for on the record: the driver accepted at 22:33:00 and cancelled at 22:42:00, so the trip ran 9 minutes and the $6.61 fee was applied under the cancellation rules in force. [F3 F6] [NS-0 NS-1]
D2: The driver did press "I'm Here" and hold position for the full five-minute stand: the timeline shows the tap at 22:37:20 and the GPS shows the car stationary from 22:37:00 to 22:42:00, i.e. more than 3 minutes of continuous waiting up to the moment of cancellation. [F5 F2 F3] [NS-1]
D3 (VOID): The driver announced arrival and asked the rider to come out, and waited roughly four more minutes before cancelling — conduct consistent with a genuine no-show attempt rather than an abusive cancellation: chat shows "Reached already, blue Toyota Prius, come out please" at 22:37 and the cancellation message at 22:41. [F8 F10 F3] [NS-1 A3]
D4: In the driver's favour on the rider's credibility, the rider's own message at 22:38 admits the rider was at the pickup point; the dispute is therefore purely about the car's position, not about whether the rider was present and waiting. [F9] [NS-1]
D5: Alternatively, if the panel treats the arrival condition as unmet, the driver is not an abusive canceller: his 90-day record shows 2 no-show disputes, both upheld (i.e. the platform has twice before confirmed no-show situations for him), which supports treating this as an operational positioning error, not a fee-gaming pattern. [F17] [NS-1]
D6: There is no evidence of any safety, threat or dangerous-driving element in this case, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not engaged and the matter can be decided on the no-show record alone. [F8 F9 F10 F12] [SAFE-1 SAFE-2]
D7: Light rain at the time (1.8 mm) is offered only as context for slower traffic and repositioning, not as an excuse: the traffic feed records no congested band and no incident on the route during the trip window. [F15 F13 F14] [NS-1 RD-4]
Weaknesses: The decisive weakness is the GPS record contradicting the driver's statement: F1 shows the closest approach to the pickup was 873 m and the driver never came within 200 m, and F5 shows the "I'm Here" tap at 22:37:20 was made 1000 m from the pickup with 0 s spent within 200 m afterwards. F2 places the car stationary 1000 m away. F4 records driver_arrived_at as null. On NS-1 (ii) and (iii) the driver plainly fails, so the record points to refund_full of $6.61 under NS-2 rather than no_action. | There is no traffic or incident record the driver can lean on to explain why the car stopped 1 km away: F14 says no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window and F13 says there are no speed band records at all, so RD-4 cannot rescue the positioning. F15 (light rain) is weak and cannot substitute for a road closure or incident. | F12 is the driver's own written statement, which is contradicted point-for-point by F1, F2, F4 and F5; under the system-records-over-statements rule it carries little weight, and the driver never states in the chat record — only after the trip — why he was 1 km from the pickup.
Asks: no_action

The driver cancelled this RydeX trip at 22:42:00 after accepting at 22:33:00, and a $6.61 cancellation fee was applied [F3][F6]. Because the driver is the cancelling party and he asserts the rider no-showed, the fee only stands if NS-1 is satisfied: the arrival confirmation, the position at that moment, and more than 3 minutes of continuous waiting at the pickup [NS-0][NS-1].

Both NS-1 conditions fail on the system record. The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 22:37:20 while 1000 m from the pickup point, and he spent 0 s within 200 m of the pickup after the tap [F5]; his closest approach at any time was 873 m and he never came within 200 m [F1]; the platform never recorded him at the pickup point at all [F4]. GPS and timeline records override the driver's written statement that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" [F12], and that statement is contradicted point-for-point by the stationary window 1000 m away [F2] and by the cancellation timeline [F3] [NS-1].

With NS-1 unmet, the fee has no basis and the $6.61 cancellation fee on the record must be returned in full to the rider — for this fixed-fare RydeX trip the whole disputed charge is that fee [F6][NS-2][NS-7]. claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 873 m at 22:36:00 and he never came within 200 m of it at any time, so the arrival condition for a no-show charge is not met.
The platform itself never recorded the driver at the pickup point — driver_arrived_at is null — so there is no arrival confirmation on the record, whether by driver tap or platform auto-detect.
The driver tapped "I'm Here" at 22:37:20 while 1000 m from the pickup point, and stayed within 200 m of it for 0 seconds after the tap, so NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both fail.

From 22:37:00 to 22:42:00 the driver was stationary 1000 m from the pickup point, so the waiting that preceded his 22:42:00 cancellation was not waiting at the pickup point; his written claim that he "waited more than 3 minutes at the pickup" is contradicted by the GPS record and by the system timeline.

At 22:38:00 the rider messaged that she was at the pickup point and saw no car, which matches the GPS record that no car was ever within 200 m, while the driver's message at 22:37:00 asserted a pick-up that the record shows never happened.
The driver cancelled 9 minutes after acceptance without any arrival at the pickup point, so the $6.61 cancellation fee charged in this case has no basis and must be refunded in full.

Because the driver pressed "I'm Here" while GPS placed him 1000 m from the pickup point, this is an abuse of the arrival/cancellation button and the account should be sent to Ryde for review; his profile shows 2 of 2 disputes upheld in the last 90 days, both no-show, supporting that request.

No traffic incident or congestion record exists on the route during the trip window, so nothing external explains the driver's failure to reach the pickup point; light rain of 1.8 mm does not place the driver 873 m away.

weaknesses: The rider herself never reached within 200 m of the car either — the record only shows she messaged "I'm at the pickup point" (F9), a rider statement, while the GPS facts (F1, F2) measure only the driver's position, so the judge cannot verify her location from a system record.
The rider's profile shows 1 dispute in 90 d with 0 upheld (F16), which the driver may use to suggest a pattern of fee challenges, though it is not evidence about this trip.

The driver can point to his 808 trips in 90 d and 4.63 rating (F17) as a reliability indicator, and to the fact that he did press "I'm Here" at 22:37:20 (F5), i.e. he at least believed he had arrived.

The chat is complete and timestamped (F11), and the driver did inform the rider at 22:37:00 (F8) and wait five more minutes before cancelling at 22:42:00 (F3) — he may argue he gave the rider ample notice, though none of that cures the missing arrival requirement.

claims.assertion: The rider was never charged a no-show fee in error on any basis the driver can be blamed for on the record: the driver accepted at 22:33:00 and cancelled at 22:42:00, so the trip ran 9 minutes and the $6.61 fee was applied under the cancellation rules in force.

The driver did press "I'm Here" and hold position for the full five-minute stand: the timeline shows the tap at 22:37:20 and the GPS shows the car stationary from 22:37:00 to 22:42:00, i.e. more than 3 minutes of continuous waiting up to the moment of cancellation.

The driver announced arrival and asked the rider to come out, and waited roughly four more minutes before cancelling — conduct consistent with a genuine no-show attempt rather than an abusive cancellation: chat shows "Reached already, blue Toyota Prius, come out please" at 22:37 and the cancellation message at 22:41.
claims.void_reason: citation check: cites A3 — not a citable clause

claims.assertion: In the driver's favour on the rider's credibility, the rider's own message at 22:38 admits the rider was at the pickup point; the dispute is therefore purely about the car's position, not about whether the rider was present and waiting.

Alternatively, if the panel treats the arrival condition as unmet, the driver is not an abusive canceller: his 90-day record shows 2 no-show disputes, both upheld (i.e. the platform has twice before confirmed no-show situations for him), which supports treating this as an operational positioning error, not a fee-gaming pattern.
There is no evidence of any safety, threat or dangerous-driving element in this case, so SAFE-1/SAFE-2 escalation is not engaged and the matter can be decided on the no-show record alone.

Light rain at the time (1.8 mm) is offered only as context for slower traffic and repositioning, not as an excuse: the traffic feed records no congested band and no incident on the route during the trip window.

weaknesses: The decisive weakness is the GPS record contradicting the driver's statement: F1 shows the closest approach to the pickup was 873 m and the driver never came within 200 m, and F5 shows the "I'm Here" tap at 22:37:20 was made 1000 m from the pickup with 0 s spent within 200 m afterwards. F2 places the car stationary 1000 m away. F4 records driver_arrived_at as null. On NS-1 (ii) and (iii) the driver plainly fails, so the record points to refund_full of $6.61 under NS-2 rather than no_action.

There is no traffic or incident record the driver can lean on to explain why the car stopped 1 km away: F14 says no traffic incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window and F13 says there are no speed band records at all, so RD-4 cannot rescue the positioning. F15 (light rain) is weak and cannot substitute for a road closure or incident.

F12 is the driver's own written statement, which is contradicted point-for-point by F1, F2, F4 and F5; under the system-records-over-statements rule it carries little weight, and the driver never states in the chat record — only after the trip — why he was 1 km from the pickup.

points.response: D1 asserts only that the fee was applied, not that it was valid: acceptance at 22:33:00 and driver cancellation at 22:42:00 (F3) with the $6.61 fee on record (F6) brings the case under NS-0, which routes a driver-side no-show allegation to NS-1 — and NS-1 requires the arrival conditions the driver fails, so the fee does not stand.

Continuous waiting at the pickup is the requirement, not continuous waiting somewhere: F5 places the 22:37:20 "I'm Here" tap 1000 m from the pickup with 0 s inside 200 m afterwards, and F2 shows the stationary car 1000 m away, so the five-minute stand occurred over 1 km from the pickup point and fails NS-1 (ii) and (iii).

The driver's own statement (F12) disputed the rider's presence, and the rider's 22:38:00 message is the rider's own account at the pickup with no car in sight (F9); the verifiable point remains the car's position, which the system record fixes 873 m away at closest and never within 200 m (F1).

The two prior upheld no-show disputes (F17) are upheld against the driver-side no-show record and cannot convert the missing arrival condition into a positioning error; they are, if anything, the repeated pattern RD-6 asks about, and the flag_account request rests on the tap 1000 m away (F5), not on the profile alone.
Conceded — no safety, threat or dangerous-driving element appears in the messages or statement (F8, F9, F10, F12), so the case is decided on the no-show record and no SAFE escalation is sought.

The traffic record leaves no reasonable cause for the reroute or reposition: F13 shows no speed bands at all and F14 shows no incidents near the route during the trip window, so 1.8 mm of light rain (F15) cannot carry RD-4.

Kept as pleaded but narrowed honestly: the flag_account request rests on the system-fact that the "I'm Here" tap was made 1000 m from the pickup (F5), not on the profile; the profile (F17) is offered only as supporting context, per the rule that profile facts never decide an issue.

Conceded on the record: F1 measures the driver's closest approach at 873 m at 22:36:00 and that he never came within 200 m, and F4 records driver_arrived_at as null, so NS-1 (ii) cannot be satisfied by any reading — the driver's only remaining position is that this was an operational positioning failure, not a deliberate fee grab.
Conceded: F4 shows driver_arrived_at is null, so no platform auto-confirmation exists; the only arrival act on the record is the driver's own tap at 22:37:20 (F5).

Conceded as to the two conditions: F5 places the tap 1000 m from the pickup with 0 s within 200 m afterwards, so NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both fail and the $6.61 cannot stand on the driver's side of the ledger.

The stationary window is conceded (F2, 22:37:00–22:42:00, 1000 m away) and F12's word "at the pickup" is not supported by the GPS; I only ask the panel to note that the wait was five real minutes until cancellation at 22:42:00 (F3) — a genuine no-show attempt made from the wrong position, not an invented one.

The record is not two-sided: F1 and F2 fix only the driver's position, and the rider's 22:38 message (F9) is a statement with no GPS fact locating her at the pickup, so the panel cannot treat her presence as a system-verified fact any more than it treats F12 as one.

A flag_account is not warranted on this record: the driver's 2 of 2 no-show disputes upheld (F17) is a history of the platform accepting his no-show reports, not of abused arrival taps, and NS-2's flag attaches to the 22:37:20 tap only as an add-on to a refund finding — the rider cites no fact showing any prior button abuse.

I withdraw the framing of D2 as compliance with NS-1: F5 shows the tap 1000 m out with 0 s inside 200 m, so the five-minute stand in F2 does not satisfy (ii) or (iii) — the correct reading is a long but misplaced wait.
